title: IoT and AI Control of Aquaponic Farms
headline: Joint PhD with UWE: a multi-sensor water-quality unit and AI models that detect anomalies and optimise an aquaponics farm, tested in a working greenhouse
photoAlt: Inside the aquaponics research greenhouse, with vertical towers, grow beds and plants
subtitle: A joint PhD with UWE that built a multi-sensor water-quality unit and used IoT data and AI to find, and hold, the best conditions for fish and plants
need: Conventional farming is under pressure from water scarcity, soil depletion, pesticide use and climate change. Aquaponics, which raises fish and grows plants in one recirculating system, uses far less water and no soil or pesticides, but it is a delicate ecosystem.

Temperature, light, airflow, dissolved oxygen, pH, ammonia and nitrate all interact. Most so-called smart aquaponics systems only compare readings against fixed limits. Commercial growers need a system that understands how these parameters affect fish and plant growth, spots problems early and keeps the farm at its best automatically.
role: SciFlair co-funded and co-supervised the PhD with the University of the West of England, and provided the IoT hardware, cloud and engineering support. The research was carried out in a working aquaponics greenhouse.
built: A multi-sensor water-quality unit: a sealed electronics enclosure with a probe head holding several water-quality probes, placed directly in the fish tank
Continuous logging of water quality and greenhouse conditions to the cloud, with a web application to view the data and send alerts
Environmental control in the greenhouse, including ventilation fans
Anomaly detection that finds patterns, correlations and trends in the sensor data and flags problems before they harm fish or plants
Optimisation models that recommend or apply corrections to water quality, nutrient flow and climate for each fish and crop combination

delivery.title: Concept
delivery.text: A literature review set out existing optimisation techniques and the key parameters to control, and defined the research questions.

delivery.title: Design and build
delivery.text: Designed and built the multi-sensor unit and its probe head, and connected it to the cloud with the greenhouse sensors and controls.

delivery.title: Field operation
delivery.text: Ran the system in a working aquaponics greenhouse with fish tanks, grow beds, deep-water lettuce rafts and vertical growing towers, collecting data across growing seasons.

delivery.title: Analysis and validation
delivery.text: Developed the anomaly detection and optimisation models from the data and validated them against further experiments and published work.

delivery.title: Completion
delivery.text: The PhD completed and the researcher graduated in 2026.
